_comment: Test vectors for the config entity format. IDs are computed by the reference implementation (Go encoding/json + crypto/sha256). Git object hashes are the ones of a SHA-1 repository.

reference.description: The config is a singleton: its reference is named after the fixed key 'config', not after its ID.

operation_pack_examples.description: First pack: the CreateOperation, which sets nothing
operation_pack_examples.note: The config ID equals the ID of this CreateOperation: hex(sha256(raw bytes of ops[0])).

operation_pack_examples.description: Second pack: set the repository description, then define and allow a label, in one edit session

ops.value: A distributed bug tracker embedded in git.

operation_pack_examples.description: Pack defining a label without color or description: fields is omitted
Pack lifting the label restriction and cleaning up a definition: the definition of 'regression' is removed, 'crash' stays defined but is no longer allowed
Pack changing only the color of 'crash': its description is unchanged
Pack clearing the description of 'crash': its color is unchanged

repo.description: A distributed bug tracker embedded in git.
A distributed bug tracker embedded in git.

labels.note: No label is allowed: any label may be used. 'regression' has no definition, and takes the color derived from its name, #cddc39.

repo.description: A distributed bug tracker embedded in git.

labels.note: The fifth pack changed the color of 'crash' and left its description as it was.

repo.description: A distributed bug tracker embedded in git.

labels.note: The sixth pack cleared the description of 'crash' and left its color as it was.

era_examples.description: The config judging an operation of another entity, by its time on the clock bugs-edit: the config operations whose times record a lower bugs-edit apply. The six packs above record bugs-edit 137, 137, 140, 151, 155 and 160.

examples.note: Every setting reads as its default: any label may be used.
As the first snapshot example: only 'crash' may be used.
'crash' and 'regression' are defined, only 'crash' may be used.

era_examples.note: times lists the first and last time of each era, the last era having no end.

derived_color_examples.description: The color of a label without one set: the palette entry at the index of the sum of the bytes of the SHA-256 of its name, modulo 19.
derived_color_examples.note: 'épique' is hashed as its UTF-8 bytes.

ordered_list_examples.description: Positions of the entries of an ordered list. No setting is an ordered list yet: these examples apply to any.

valid_positions.note: integer part a0, empty fractional part
integer part a0, fractional part V
integer part Zz, the one just below a0
integer part b12: b gives a length of 3
the smallest integer part, with a fractional part

invalid_positions.note: a gives an integer part of 2 characters, only 1 is there
b gives an integer part of 3 characters, only 2 are there
the fractional part V0 ends with 0
the first character is not a letter
A followed by 26 0, with nothing after it

sort_example.note: By position, compared byte by byte; p and q share a position and are listed by key; m and n have no position and come last, by key.

tie_example.description: Alice and Bob concurrently insert p and q between x (a0) and y (a1), and both pick a0V. Carol then inserts r between p and q: as no position lies between theirs, her pack first moves q.

pack.note: move q between p (a0V) and y (a1)
insert r between p (a0V) and q (a0l)

tie_example.note: a0l and a0d are what Greenspan's midpoint gives; any position between the neighbours is as valid.

id_derivation.description: Config ID equals the ID of its CreateOperation: hex(sha256(raw bytes of ops[0])) in the first pack.
id_derivation.note: raw is ops[0] of the first pack as written in git: compact JSON, with the keys in this order. expected_id is the SHA-256 of raw.
